1. 잠언을 기록한 목적\n 1) 솔로몬이 가장 지혜와 명철이 뛰어났을:
1. Why Proverbs was written
 1) Solomon wrote it when he was at the height of his wisdom and understanding. The word for proverb in Hebrew is mashal, and you can think of it as Solomon's wise sayings.
짤막한 글귀로 대체로 대구법으로 기록되어 있음.\n 2) 솔로몬이 300:
They're short sayings, mostly written in parallelism, where two lines mirror each other.
 2) Solomon wrote some 3,000 proverbs, but not all of them made it into the Bible. What we have now as Proverbs is what King Hezekiah's officials edited and selected. They edited it once, then a second time. That's why some parts repeat.
<잠25:1> 이것도 솔로몬의 잠언이요 유다 왕 히스기야의 신하들의 편집:
<Prov 25:1> These also are proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
 3) Solomon had so many wives that he couldn't teach all his kids one by one, so it seems he wrote these proverbs so the women could use them to teach the children. If you look at the end, there's a proverb about a woman.
<잠1:1~6> 다윗의 아들 이스라엘 왕 솔로몬의 잠언이라 이는 ①지혜와:
<Prov 1:1~6> The proverbs of Solomon, the son of David, king of Israel: ① to know wisdom and instruction; ② to discern the words of understanding; ③ to receive instruction in wise dealing, in righteousness, justice, and equity; ④ to give prudence to the simple, ⑤ knowledge and discretion to the young man: ⑥ that the wise man may hear, and increase in learning; that the man of understanding may attain to sound counsel: to understand a proverb, and parables, the words and riddles of the wise.
- This tells us why Proverbs was written.
 4) God hears our prayers only when we listen to His law.
<잠28:9> 사람이 귀를 돌이키고 율법을 듣지 아니하면 그의 기도도 가: <Prov 28:9> He who turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer is an abomination.
